questions.question: A forecasting technique in which a panel of experts gives estimates anonymously, receives a summary of the group's answers, and revises its estimates over several rounds until a consensus emerges is the
questions.explanation: The Delphi method is a structured form of expert opinion that uses anonymous, repeated rounds of estimates and feedback. Option A uses the firm's salespeople, Option B uses real sales in a test area, and Option C multiplies a base number by a series of percentages to estimate potential.

questions.question: A Lagos snack company launches its new plantain chips only in Ibadan for three months, records actual purchases there, and uses the results to estimate national demand. Which forecasting method is this?
questions.explanation: A market test puts the product on sale in a limited area and uses the real buying response to forecast wider demand, which is especially useful for new products. Option D relies on stated plans rather than actual purchases, Option C on expert judgement, and Option A on averaging past sales that a new product does not yet have.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four components into which past sales (time series) are usually broken down?
questions.explanation: Time-series analysis splits past sales into trend, cycle, season and erratic events. Elasticity measures how demand responds to price changes; it is not a time-series component. Option A, Option C and Option B are all genuine components.

questions.question: Sales of umbrellas and raincoats in Lagos rise every year between April and July and fall in the dry season. In time-series analysis this repeated pattern within the year is the
questions.explanation: A seasonal component is a consistent pattern of sales movements within the year, linked to weather, holidays or similar factors. Option A is the long-run basic growth or decline, Option D is the medium-term wave linked to the business cycle, and Option B covers unpredictable one-off events.

questions.question: A transport company's ticket sales drop sharply for two weeks because of an unexpected fuel scarcity and then recover. In time-series analysis this unusual drop is part of the
questions.explanation: Erratic events are unpredictable disruptions such as strikes, riots or shortages; they are removed from past data so the normal pattern can be seen. Option C is the long-term direction, Option D repeats every year, and Option B follows the wave-like movement of the general economy over several years.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using a moving average when forecasting sales?

options.a: To combine the opinions of a panel of experts
options.b: To smooth out short-term, random fluctuations in past sales so the underlying level is clearer
options.c: To measure how customers respond to a change in price
options.d: To estimate the share of the market held by competitors

questions.explanation: A moving average replaces individual sales figures with the average of the most recent periods, which smooths out random ups and downs. Option C describes price elasticity, Option A describes expert opinion or Delphi, and Option D describes market share analysis.

questions.question: How does a weighted moving average differ from a simple moving average?

options.a: It ignores past sales and uses buyers' stated intentions
options.b: It gives different weights to the periods, usually more weight to the most recent ones
options.c: It uses only the oldest period in the data
options.d: It always uses more periods than a simple moving average

questions.explanation: A simple moving average gives every period equal weight, while a weighted moving average attaches larger weights to more recent periods so the forecast reacts faster to change. Option C and Option D are not what defines the weighted method, and Option A describes a survey of buyers' intentions.

questions.question: Trend projection as a forecasting method is based on the main assumption that

options.a: experts' opinions are always more accurate than data
options.b: the pattern of past sales will continue into the future
options.c: the market is completely new and has no history
options.d: buyers will always do exactly what they say in surveys

questions.explanation: Trend projection fits a line or growth rate to past data and extends it forward, so it assumes past patterns continue. It can mislead when there is a sudden change in the environment. Option D relates to buyer-intention surveys, Option C would make trend projection impossible, and Option A relates to judgement methods.

questions.question: A method of estimating market potential that starts with a base number (such as population) and multiplies it by a series of percentages that narrow it down to likely buyers is called the
questions.explanation: The chain-ratio method multiplies a base figure by several adjusting percentages, for example population x share of adults x share who drink the product. Option A adds up potential buyers identified market by market, Option B is an expert-opinion technique, and Option C is a time-series smoothing method.

questions.question: Identifying all the potential buyers in each market (for example, every bakery in a state) and estimating their potential purchases, then adding these up, is known as the
questions.explanation: The market-buildup method builds total potential from a list of identifiable buyers and their likely purchases; it is common in business markets. Option C works down from a base number using percentages, Option A collects salespeople's sales estimates, and Option D measures actual sales in a test area.

questions.question: In market measurement, the 'available market' is best described as

options.a: the set of consumers who have already bought the product
options.b: the set of consumers who have interest in, income for and access to a particular offer
options.c: all consumers who profess any level of interest, regardless of income or access
options.d: the part of the market the company has decided to pursue

questions.explanation: The available market consists of consumers who have interest, income and access to the offer. Option A is the penetrated market, Option D is the target (served) market, and Option C is the potential market, which ignores whether buyers can afford or reach the product.

questions.question: A market has 2,000,000 potential buyers. Each buyer purchases an average of 4 units of a detergent per year at an average price of N1,500 per unit. Using Q = n x q x p, what is the total market potential per year?
questions.explanation: Total market potential Q = n x q x p = 2,000,000 x 4 x N1,500 = N12,000,000,000. Option D multiplies only buyers by price and forgets the 4 units each buyer purchases. Option A is a decimal slip (one zero lost), and Option B is the number of units multiplied out without the price.

questions.question: In a town, 50,000 households each buy 3 loaves of bread per week at N1,200 per loaf. Assuming 52 weeks in a year, what is the annual market potential for bread in naira?
questions.explanation: Annual quantity per household = 3 x 52 = 156 loaves, so market potential = 50,000 x 156 x N1,200 = N9,360,000,000. Option C is only one week's spending. Option B wrongly treats 3 loaves a week as 3 loaves a month (x12), and Option D uses 48 weeks instead of the 52 stated.

questions.question: Using the market-buildup method, a flour miller identifies 400 bakeries in its state. Each bakery buys an average of 20 bags of flour a month at N60,000 per bag. What is the annual market potential in the state?
questions.explanation: Annual bags = 400 x 20 x 12 = 96,000, so potential = 96,000 x N60,000 = N5,760,000,000. Option B is only one month's purchases (it forgets to multiply by 12), and Option C uses 6 months instead of 12.

questions.question: Using the chain-ratio method: a city has 1,200,000 people; 60% are adults; 40% of adults drink malt drinks; and each malt drinker consumes 50 bottles a year. What is the estimated annual market potential in bottles?
questions.explanation: Chain ratio: 1,200,000 x 0.60 x 0.40 x 50 = 14,400,000 bottles. Option D skips the 60% adult ratio, Option B skips the 40% malt-drinker ratio, and Option C gives the number of drinkers (288,000) but forgets to multiply by 50 bottles each.

questions.question: In a year, a paint company sold goods worth N45 million, while total sales of all paint companies in the same market (including this company) were N300 million. What is the company's market share?
questions.explanation: Market share = company sales / total market sales x 100 = 45 / 300 x 100 = 15%. Option A is the share held by all competitors together. Option B wrongly adds the company's sales to a total that already includes them, giving 45 / 345.

questions.question: A juice brand sold 42,000 cartons in a quarter. Total industry sales in the same market and quarter were 168,000 cartons (including the brand's sales). What is the brand's market share in volume terms?
questions.explanation: Volume market share = 42,000 / 168,000 x 100 = 25%. Option D is the competitors' combined share, Option C divides by 168,000 + 42,000 and so double counts the brand, and Option B divides the wrong way round.

questions.question: Total market demand for cement in a region next year is forecast at N800 million. A company expects to hold a 12% market share. What is its sales forecast for the year?
questions.explanation: Company sales forecast = market demand x expected market share = N800m x 0.12 = N96 million. Option B misplaces the decimal, Option C gives the competitors' expected sales (88%), and Option D divides by 12 instead of taking 12%.

questions.question: Relative market share is defined as a firm's market share divided by the market share of its largest competitor. Firm A has a 20% market share and its largest competitor has 40%. What is Firm A's relative market share?
questions.explanation: Relative market share = 20% / 40% = 0.5, meaning Firm A is half the size of the leader. Option B divides the wrong way round. Option D takes the difference between the shares instead of the ratio.

questions.question: Relative market share is defined as a firm's market share divided by that of its largest competitor. A market leader holds 36% of the market and the next-largest firm holds 24%. What is the leader's relative market share?
questions.explanation: For the leader, the largest competitor is the 24% firm, so relative share = 36 / 24 = 1.5. A value above 1 shows the firm leads the market. Option A inverts the ratio, and Option C uses the difference in percentage points instead of a ratio.

questions.question: The market penetration index is defined as current market demand divided by market potential, expressed as a percentage. If current demand for solar lanterns in a state is 6 million units and market potential is 15 million units, what is the market penetration index?
questions.explanation: Penetration index = 6 / 15 x 100 = 40%. A low index suggests large room for market growth. Option B divides the wrong way round, and Option D is the unpenetrated part of the potential (60%).

questions.question: Monthly sales (in thousands of units) of a product for January to June were 40, 46, 48, 55, 51 and 57. Using a 3-month simple moving average, what is the sales forecast for July? (to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: A 3-month moving average forecast uses the latest three months: (55 + 51 + 57) / 3 = 54.33 thousand. Option A averages all six months, Option B averages the first three months instead of the latest three, and Option C simply repeats June's figure.

questions.question: Quarterly sales (N million) for five consecutive quarters were 120, 135, 128, 142 and 150. Using a 4-quarter simple moving average, what is the forecast for the next quarter? (to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: The 4-quarter moving average uses the four most recent quarters: (135 + 128 + 142 + 150) / 4 = 138.75. Option A averages all five quarters, Option C uses the four oldest quarters, and Option B adds the right four quarters but divides by 5.

questions.question: Sales for the last three months (oldest first) were 120, 130 and 150 units. Using a weighted moving average with weights of 3 for the most recent month, 2 for the month before and 1 for the oldest month, what is next month's forecast? (to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: WMA = (3 x 150 + 2 x 130 + 1 x 120) / (3 + 2 + 1) = 830 / 6 = 138.33. Option A applies the heaviest weight to the oldest month, Option D is the simple (unweighted) average, and Option B divides by the number of months (3) instead of the sum of the weights (6).

questions.question: A firm's trend line for annual sales is Y = 200 + 15X, where Y is sales in thousands of units and X = 1 for 2019, 2 for 2020, and so on. What is the forecast for 2026?
questions.explanation: 2026 is the 8th year when 2019 is X = 1, so Y = 200 + 15(8) = 320. Option C uses X = 7 (counting the years wrongly), Option B uses X = 1, and Option D wrongly multiplies the whole of (200 + 15) by 8.

questions.question: Sales (N million) for 2021 to 2025 were 20, 24, 27, 31 and 33. Using the least-squares trend Y = a + bX with X coded -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 (so that sum of X = 0, a = sum of Y / n and b = sum of XY / sum of X^2), what is the forecast for 2026? (to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanation: a = 135 / 5 = 27; b = sum XY / sum X^2 = 33 / 10 = 3.3. 2026 is coded X = 3, so Y = 27 + 3.3(3) = 36.9. Option D uses X = 5 (forgetting the coding is centred on 2023), Option B gives only the average a, and Option A uses X = 1, which is the 2024 trend value.

questions.question: A firm's sales (thousand units) for five years were 50, 56, 59, 65 and 70. With the years coded X = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, the least-squares slope is b = sum of XY / sum of X^2. What is the value of b, the average yearly increase in the trend? (to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanation: Sum XY = -100 - 56 + 0 + 65 + 140 = 49, and sum X^2 = 4 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 4 = 10, so b = 49 / 10 = 4.9. Option C divides by n = 5 instead of sum X^2, Option B divides the total change by 5 years instead of 4 intervals, and Option A is the intercept a, not the slope.

questions.question: A firm's sales were N100 million in 2021 and N140 million in 2025. Assuming sales continue to grow by the same average amount each year (a straight-line trend), what is the forecast for 2026?
questions.explanation: There are 4 yearly intervals from 2021 to 2025, so the average annual increase = (140 - 100) / 4 = N10 million and the 2026 forecast = 140 + 10 = N150 million. Option A wrongly divides by 5 (counting years instead of intervals). Option D adds the whole four-year increase, and Option B is just the average of the two years.

questions.question: A company's sales this year are N50 million. If sales are expected to grow at a constant 10% per year (compound growth), what is the forecast for two years from now? (to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanation: Compound growth: 50 x (1.1)^2 = N60.5 million. Option B uses simple growth (10% of the original N50m each year), which ignores growth on the first year's increase. Option A is only one year ahead, and Option D is three years ahead.

questions.question: A survey of buyers' intentions in a market of 200,000 households finds that 15% will 'definitely buy' a new water purifier next year and 25% will 'probably buy'. Past experience shows that 80% of 'definite' and 20% of 'probable' respondents actually buy. How many households are expected to buy?
questions.explanation: Expected buying rate = 0.15 x 0.80 + 0.25 x 0.20 = 0.12 + 0.05 = 0.17, so buyers = 200,000 x 0.17 = 34,000. Option B assumes everyone who said 'definitely' or 'probably' will buy. Option D uses only the 'definite' group without adjustment, and Option C ignores the 'probable' group.

questions.question: Three sales representatives estimate next year's sales in their territories at 40,000, 55,000 and 65,000 units. Management believes the team is usually over-optimistic and reduces the combined estimate by 10%. What is the sales-force composite forecast?
questions.explanation: Composite = 40,000 + 55,000 + 65,000 = 160,000 units, then reduce by 10%: 160,000 x 0.90 = 144,000. Option B forgets management's adjustment, Option D averages the territories instead of adding them, and Option C increases rather than reduces the estimate.

questions.question: Three experts forecast next year's industry sales at N120 million, N150 million and N135 million. The firm gives their opinions weights of 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2 respectively based on past accuracy. What is the weighted expert-opinion forecast?
questions.explanation: Weighted forecast = 0.5(120) + 0.3(150) + 0.2(135) = 60 + 45 + 27 = N132 million. Option A is the simple average that ignores the weights, Option B adds the forecasts without averaging, and Option C attaches the weights to the wrong experts.

questions.question: In a market test, a new seasoning cube sold 30,000 packs in a test city that contains 2% of the national target population. Assuming the test city is representative, what is the estimated national sales?
questions.explanation: If 2% of the population bought 30,000 packs, the whole population would buy 30,000 / 0.02 = 1,500,000 packs. Option A multiplies by 2% instead of dividing, Option C treats 2% as 0.2, and Option D treats 2% as 0.002.

questions.question: A buying power index for a state is calculated as 0.5(state's % share of national disposable income) + 0.3(% share of national retail sales) + 0.2(% share of national population). A state has 4% of income, 5% of retail sales and 3% of population. If national market potential is N500 billion, what is the state's market potential?
questions.explanation: BPI = 0.5(4) + 0.3(5) + 0.2(3) = 2.0 + 1.5 + 0.6 = 4.1%, so state potential = 4.1% x N500bn = N20.5 billion. Option B uses a simple unweighted average of 4%, Option D uses retail sales share alone, and Option A attaches the weights to the wrong factors (3.8%).

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: The use of digital channels and technologies, such as websites, search engines, social media, email and mobile apps, to promote products and engage customers is broadly known as
questions.explanation: Digital marketing covers all marketing activities carried out through digital channels and devices. Option C is face-to-face selling by a sales force, Option A uses billboards and similar physical media, and Option D targets resellers with offers such as trade allowances.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: E-marketing (internet marketing) is best described as

options.a: marketing products and services over the internet, through websites, online ads, email and similar tools
options.b: selling products only through door-to-door salespeople
options.c: advertising only on radio and television

questions.explanation: E-marketing refers to marketing activities conducted over the internet, such as company websites, online advertising and email. Option B is personal selling, Option C is traditional broadcast advertising, and Option D is traditional direct mail.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Using platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X (Twitter) and LinkedIn to build brand awareness, interact with customers and promote offers is called
questions.explanation: Social media marketing uses social networking platforms to reach, engage and build relationships with customers. Option D uses telephone calls, Option B is aimed at wholesalers and retailers, and Option A sends printed offers to addresses.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of online advertising?

options.a: A handbill distributed at a bus stop
options.b: A banner ad for a hotel appearing on a Nigerian news website
options.c: A jingle played on a market loudspeaker
options.d: A billboard on Third Mainland Bridge

questions.explanation: Online advertising is paid promotional content shown on the internet, such as display banners, search ads, social media ads and video ads. Option D, Option A and Option C are traditional offline promotion methods that do not use the internet.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: What is the main difference between search engine optimisation (SEO) and pay-per-click (PPC) search advertising?

options.a: SEO is only used on television, while PPC is used online
options.b: SEO and PPC both refer to sending bulk SMS messages
options.c: SEO aims to improve a website's free (organic) ranking in search results, while PPC buys sponsored listings and pays each time the ad is clicked
options.d: SEO is paid per click, while PPC is always free

questions.explanation: SEO improves a site's content and structure so it ranks higher in unpaid (organic) results, while PPC places paid ads in search results and charges the advertiser per click. Option D reverses the two, and Option A and Option B describe neither technique.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Lagos online furniture store bids on keywords such as 'office chairs Lagos' so that its sponsored link appears at the top of search results, and it pays only when someone clicks the ad. This is
questions.explanation: Pay-per-click search advertising lets advertisers bid on keywords and pay only when users click the ad. Option B improves unpaid rankings rather than buying ad space, Option C pays partners commission for sales they refer, and Option D attracts customers with useful free content.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Creating and sharing valuable, relevant material such as blog posts, how-to videos and infographics, in order to attract and engage a clearly defined audience rather than directly pushing a sales message, is called
questions.explanation: Content marketing earns attention by giving the audience useful or entertaining content, which builds trust and eventually sales. Option D is face-to-face persuasion, Option C is short-term incentives such as discounts, and Option B is selling over the phone.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Nigerian skincare brand publishes free weekly videos on how to care for skin in hot, humid weather, without directly asking viewers to buy. The brand is mainly using
questions.explanation: Providing helpful, relevant content to attract and keep an audience is content marketing. Option D is a price tactic, Option B involves salespeople meeting customers, and Option C targets wholesalers and retailers rather than consumers.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Partnering with individuals who have a large or highly engaged online following, such as content creators and celebrities, so that they recommend a brand to their followers is called
questions.explanation: Influencer marketing uses people whose opinions their followers trust to promote a brand. Option B uses phone calls, Option A uses printed mail, and Option C uses trade fairs and exhibitions.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Compared with celebrity or 'mega' influencers, micro-influencers are generally described as having

options.a: no followers at all, since they only use paid ads
options.b: the largest possible audiences across many unrelated interests
options.c: audiences made up only of business buyers
options.d: smaller, more focused audiences that often show higher engagement and trust

questions.explanation: Micro-influencers have smaller followings, often within a specific niche, and their followers tend to engage more and trust them more. Option B describes mega or celebrity influencers. Option A and Option C do not describe influencers at all.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Marketing messages, promotions and other content delivered to consumers through their mobile phones, such as SMS, in-app ads and mobile websites, is called
questions.explanation: Mobile marketing reaches consumers on their mobile devices through text messages, apps, mobile ads and mobile web. Option C uses billboards and posters, Option B uses printed catalogues, and Option A targets resellers.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Nigerian supermarket sends text messages to customers' phones announcing a weekend discount, to customers who gave their numbers at checkout. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Sending promotional text messages to customers' phones is SMS marketing, a form of mobile marketing. Option A is outdoor advertising, Option C involves a salesperson interacting with the buyer, and Option D builds goodwill and manages publicity rather than sending direct offers.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A restaurant in Ikeja sends a discount offer to customers' phones only when their app shows they are within 1 kilometre of the restaurant. This technique is known as
questions.explanation: Location-based mobile marketing uses the phone's location to send relevant offers to people nearby. Option D improves website rankings in search results, Option A targets resellers, and Option B uses physical mail rather than real-time phone location.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Sending marketing messages only to consumers who have agreed (opted in) to receive them, for example by subscribing to a newsletter, is known as
questions.explanation: Permission-based marketing sends messages only to people who have opted in, which improves relevance and trust. Option D is unsolicited and unwanted commercial messaging, the opposite of permission. Option A uses unconventional low-cost tactics, and Option C means contacting people who have not asked to be contacted.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Unsolicited, unwanted commercial email messages sent in bulk to people who did not ask for them are commonly called
questions.explanation: Spam is unwanted bulk commercial messaging; it annoys recipients and can damage a brand's reputation. Option B is valuable content that attracts an audience, Option C is free publicity or sharing by others, and Option A is content created by customers themselves.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A marketing message designed to be so entertaining or useful that people pass it on to friends rapidly online, the digital version of word-of-mouth, is called
questions.explanation: Viral marketing creates content that people want to share, so it spreads quickly from person to person at low cost. Option A targets resellers, Option B sets sales targets for a sales force, and Option C uses telephone calls.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Photos, videos, reviews and posts about a brand that are created and shared by customers rather than by the company itself are called
questions.explanation: User-generated content (UGC) is brand-related content produced by consumers, such as reviews or unboxing videos. Option A is created and controlled by the firm, Option C is space the firm pays for, and Option D are displays prepared by the firm for stores.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A brand's own website, Instagram page and company blog are classified as which type of media?
questions.explanation: Owned media are channels the company itself controls, such as its website and official social pages. Option A is space the brand buys, such as sponsored posts, Option D is free coverage or sharing generated by others, and Option C refers to radio and television.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Nigerian food blogger, without being paid, posts a glowing review of a new Lekki restaurant, and thousands of people share it. For the restaurant, this exposure is
questions.explanation: Earned media is publicity the brand did not pay for or create, such as unpaid reviews, shares and mentions. Option C would require the restaurant to pay for the placement, Option B is the restaurant's own channels, and Option A is a short-term incentive such as a discount.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A fashion brand pays to 'boost' (sponsor) its Instagram post so that it appears in the feeds of 50,000 targeted users. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Paid media is exposure the brand buys, such as sponsored or boosted posts and online ads. Option B is free exposure from others, Option D is the brand's own channels without paying for extra reach, and Option A is content created by customers.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Positive or negative comments about products and brands that consumers share with each other through reviews, social media posts and online forums are called
questions.explanation: Electronic word-of-mouth is consumer-to-consumer talk about brands that takes place online and can spread very widely. Option A is selling by a firm's sales force, Option C is incentives given to resellers, and Option D are sales targets.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A business pays a commission to bloggers or website owners for each sale made through a special link or code they share with their audience. This is
questions.explanation: In affiliate marketing, partners promote a firm's products and earn a commission on each sale traced to their links or codes. Option A improves organic search rankings, Option B manages publicity and goodwill, and Option D uses billboards and posters.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A student browses a laptop on an online store but leaves without buying. Over the next few days, ads for that same laptop keep appearing on other websites and social media she visits. This tactic is called
questions.explanation: Retargeting shows ads to people who have already visited a website or viewed a product, reminding them to return. Option D relies on people sharing content voluntarily, Option B is a forecasting method using a test area, and Option A involves direct contact with a salesperson.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Buying and selling directly within social media platforms, for example a vendor displaying products in a WhatsApp Business catalogue and taking orders in the chat, is known as
questions.explanation: Social commerce is the use of social networks to sell products, so discovery, conversation and ordering all happen on the platform. Option D targets resellers, Option B uses phone calls, and Option C refers to selling to businesses rather than a selling method on social platforms.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes social media marketing from traditional mass-media advertising such as newspaper ads?

options.a: Two-way, interactive communication in which customers can reply, comment and share
options.b: Results that cannot be measured at all
options.c: One-way communication with no customer response
options.d: Messages that can never be targeted to particular groups

questions.explanation: Social media allows a conversation: customers can respond, comment, share and even create content, and brands can reply in real time. Option C describes traditional mass media. Option D and Option B are wrong because social media allows precise targeting and detailed measurement.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which of the following is a key ADVANTAGE of digital marketing over most traditional media?

options.a: It does not allow any targeting by interest or age
options.b: Results such as clicks, views and sales can be measured precisely and quickly
options.c: Every customer must visit a physical shop to see the message
options.d: It can only reach people in one location

questions.explanation: Digital channels track impressions, clicks, conversions and costs in near real time, so marketers can measure performance and adjust campaigns. Option C, Option D and Option A are limitations that digital marketing actually overcomes through online reach and precise targeting.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of digital and social media marketing for a small business in Nigeria?

options.a: It guarantees that no customer will ever post a negative comment
options.b: It allows targeting by location, age and interests
options.c: It allows quick, two-way interaction with customers
options.d: It can reach many customers at relatively low cost

questions.explanation: Digital marketing does not protect a business from negative comments; in fact, criticism can spread quickly online, which is one of its challenges. Option D, Option B and Option C are genuine advantages: low cost, precise targeting and interactivity.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which of the following is a major CHALLENGE of digital marketing in Nigeria?

options.a: Online results can never be measured
options.b: Digital ads can never be targeted to particular groups
options.d: The cost of mobile data and unreliable power supply can limit how often some customers go online

questions.explanation: The cost of internet data, uneven network coverage and unreliable electricity can limit how often some consumers are online, which reduces the reach of digital campaigns. Option B and Option A are false because digital ads are targetable and measurable, and Option C is plainly untrue given widespread mobile phone use.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Why is online fraud and lack of trust considered a challenge for e-marketing in Nigeria?

options.a: It makes internet advertising completely free
options.b: Some consumers fear being scammed and hesitate to pay online or share personal details, which slows online sales
options.c: It increases the number of honest online buyers
options.d: It forces every business to stop using social media

questions.explanation: Fear of scams, fake vendors and misuse of personal data can make consumers reluctant to buy or pay online, so businesses must work to build trust, for example with pay-on-delivery and secure payment options. Option A, Option C and Option D do not describe genuine effects of online fraud.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A customer posts a video complaint about a Lagos bakery's spoiled cake, and within hours it is shared thousands of times. This illustrates which challenge of social media marketing?

options.a: Social media cannot reach young people
options.b: Social media communication is strictly one-way
options.c: Negative messages can spread quickly and are difficult for the firm to control
options.d: Social media posts cannot be shared

questions.explanation: On social media, consumers control much of the conversation, and a single complaint can spread rapidly and damage a brand's reputation, so firms need to monitor and respond quickly. Option A, Option B and Option D are false: social media reaches young people, is two-way, and is built for sharing.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Seeing very many ads online can cause some consumers to install ad blockers or simply ignore banner ads. This problem is best described as
questions.explanation: When consumers are exposed to too many ads, they tune them out or block them, which reduces the effectiveness of online advertising. Option B is dividing a market into groups, Option D is face-to-face selling, and Option A is charging different prices to different buyers.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which statement best compares digital marketing with traditional marketing?

options.a: Digital marketing reaches fewer people than traditional marketing in every case
options.b: Traditional marketing allows customers to comment and share instantly, while digital marketing does not
options.c: There is no difference between them in targeting or measurement
options.d: Digital marketing allows more precise targeting, real-time measurement and interaction, while traditional marketing relies more on one-way mass media such as print, radio and TV

questions.explanation: Digital marketing is interactive, measurable and can be targeted at precise audiences, while traditional media mostly broadcast one message to a mass audience. Option A is not always true, Option B reverses the two, and Option C ignores the clear differences.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Nigerian telecoms brand creates a branded hashtag and invites customers to post short dance videos using it, with the best entries winning data bundles. The main aim of this activity is to

options.a: generate engagement and user-generated content that spreads the brand message
options.b: reduce the brand's need for any customers
options.c: replace all of the brand's distribution channels
options.d: set sales quotas for the brand's salespeople

questions.explanation: Hashtag challenges encourage customers to participate, create content and share it, increasing engagement and reach at relatively low cost. Option B, Option C and Option D are not purposes of a social media campaign.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: An online banner ad for a Lagos hotel was shown 80,000 times (impressions) and clicked 1,200 times. Click-through rate (CTR) = clicks / impressions x 100. What is the CTR?
questions.explanation: CTR = 1,200 / 80,000 x 100 = 1.5%. Option B forgets to multiply by 100, Option A divides impressions by clicks, the wrong way round, and Option D multiplies by 1,000 instead of 100.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A brand pays N90,000 for an online display campaign that delivers 600,000 impressions. Cost per thousand impressions (CPM) = total cost / impressions x 1,000. What is the CPM?
questions.explanation: CPM = N90,000 / 600,000 x 1,000 = N150. Option D is the cost per single impression (N0.15) because it forgets the x 1,000. Option B multiplies by 10,000 instead of 1,000, and Option A divides impressions by cost, the wrong way round.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: An online fashion store spent N75,000 on pay-per-click ads in a month and received 2,500 clicks. What was the average cost per click (CPC = total ad spend / number of clicks)?
questions.explanation: CPC = N75,000 / 2,500 = N30 per click. Option C divides clicks by spend, the wrong way round. Option B and Option D are place-value slips of 100 and 10.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Nigerian e-commerce page received 4,000 visitors from a social media campaign, and 120 of them placed an order. Conversion rate = orders / visitors x 100. What is the conversion rate?
questions.explanation: Conversion rate = 120 / 4,000 x 100 = 3%. Option B forgets to multiply by 100, Option A divides the wrong way round, and Option C multiplies by 1,000 instead of 100.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: An influencer with 25,000 followers posts a sponsored video that receives 900 likes, 250 comments and 350 shares. If engagement rate = (likes + comments + shares) / followers x 100, what is the engagement rate?
questions.explanation: Total engagements = 900 + 250 + 350 = 1,500, so engagement rate = 1,500 / 25,000 x 100 = 6%. Option D counts only likes, Option C forgets to multiply by 100, and Option A divides the wrong way round.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: A Lagos cosmetics seller spent N400,000 on Instagram ads and traced N1,800,000 of sales revenue to those ads. Return on ad spend (ROAS) = revenue from ads / ad spend. What is the ROAS?
questions.explanation: ROAS = N1,800,000 / N400,000 = 4.5, meaning each N1 of advertising brought in N4.50 of sales. Option C divides the wrong way round, Option B subtracts the ad spend first, which is the profit-style return rather than ROAS as defined, and Option D wrongly multiplies by 100.

questions.topic: Marketing in the Digital and Social Media Era
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of digital marketing?

options.b: Optimising a website to rank higher on search engines
options.c: Sending an email newsletter to subscribers
options.d: Painting a shop's name and products on a roadside wall

questions.explanation: Painting a roadside wall is traditional outdoor promotion and uses no digital channel. Option C is email marketing, Option A is paid social media advertising, and Option B is search engine optimisation, all of which are forms of digital marketing.
